reports.summary: ROOT-CAUSE OF THE SPACES/OVERFLOW BUG: The user's "spaces render as DOUBLE/TRIPLE/FIVE spaces" is a MISDIAGNOSIS of the symptom. VERIFIED: (a) the batch data contains only SINGLE spaces in dialogue/narration (only 22 of 14,136 english entries have multi-spaces, and those are intentional column alignment like "Yes  No" or shop price tables); (b) the R1188 dialogue/narration font atlas is BYTE-IDENTICAL across v86/v87/v89 (md5 1f6b404e05) so the space glyph width did NOT change; (c) the "The cheers / echoed through / the tavern" group is BYTE-IDENTICAL in v87 and v89 (raw words "0034 0048 0045 0000 ..." = single 0x0000 space glyphs) yet renders with wide gaps on screen. CONCLUSION: the wide inter-word gap is the LONG-STANDING proportional/centered rendering of R1188's space glyph (slot 0) — NOT a v89 regression and NOT extra space glyphs. The build_v9 Step 4 encoder does NOT inject extra spaces (split on ' / ' and ' // ' correctly strips delimiter spaces; per-char loop encodes only the single literal spaces present). THE ACTUAL OVERFLOW REGRESSION has two real, verified causes: (1) The game does NOT auto-wrap — it renders each ' / '-delimited line CENTERED and clips at the box edge. Dialogue/narration lines authored as long unbroken strings overflow. build_v9 Step 4 (type-02 path, lines 297-319) does NOT call word_wrap() — word_wrap is only applied to the type-01/R34/R35 path at line 149. 2,604 dialogue lines exceed 18 glyphs after ' / ' splitting (R1208:858, R1209:580, R1199:171, etc.), and the NEW v89 choice-attached narration lines (e.g. R1197 m916 "The woman knight hangs her head." = 32 chars, one line) overflow. (2) The choice/portrait-aware injector PREPENDS a leading portrait control word (0xFFF0) to the question glyph stream — VERIFIED in R1197 g917: raw "FFF0 0025 0056 0045 004E ... " decodes to "<CFFF0>Even the way<LF>she stood<LF>...". At runtime the game renders the unrecognized 0xFFF0 as placeholder glyphs, which is the on-screen "AAA" prefix in the after-chargen overflow screenshot. The R2880 intro prologue (separate texture, md5 CHANGED v86->v87->v89) is an independent regression: the 18 English lines are long sentences split mid-sentence across fixed bands and the page is displayed zoomed/panned so right content clips ("the kingdc", "would be remembe", "into bloo").

R1251/1250/1252/1253 are byte-identical JP-vs-v89 (md5 match). The reason some v89 screenshots show NO portrait is that the R1251 portrait is a large faded character FIGURE that animates/fades in and out per-moment within a dialogue — it is uploaded to 0x3000, drawn, then 0x3000 is reused by the 256x64 speaker-name-box and the 512x256 R1188 font atlas in the SAME frame. So there is no regression: every artifact that could carry a portrait trigger is byte-clean (EXE, Section-1, R1251). There is no static trigger to fix; the figure's appearance is a runtime fade-animation phase. RECOMMENDATION: stop treating 'missing portrait' as a build bug. If the user genuinely wants the figure more visible, that is an engine animation/alpha behavior present in original JP too — not something our PACKDATA/EXE changes broke. The only decisive remaining test is an EE breakpoint on the R1251 BITBLT in original-JP vs v89 at the IDENTICAL in-game moment; but cross-build VRAM identity already makes a build regression extremely unlikely.
